issue.title: Race between ` PyUnicode_SET_UTF8` and `_PyUnicode_CheckConsistency`

labels.name: type-bug
labels.description: An unexpected behavior, bug, or error

issue.body:
# Bug report

### Bug description:

Reproducible by running : 

1. `env CC=clang CXX=clang++ ./configure --disable-gil --with-thread-sanitizer --with-pydebug && make -j`
2. `env TSAN_OPTIONS=suppressions=${PWD}/Tools/tsan/suppressions_free_threading.txt ./python -m test --tsan test_importlib --match test_multiprocessing_pool_circular_import -F`

comments.body: I think the right solution might be to acquire a critical section on `op` around the body of `_PyUnicode_CheckConsistency`.

I'd lean towards making this an a relaxed atomic load in `_PyUnicode_CheckConsistency`.

I'd like to avoid critical sections in `_PyUnicode_CheckConsistency` both because of performance considerations and because it may introduce subtle behavioral changes in code paths that did not lock before. (For example, a critical section may allow for a stop-the-world pause in a place where it was not possible before.)

> I'd lean towards making this an a relaxed atomic load in _PyUnicode_CheckConsistency. I'd like to avoid critical sections in _PyUnicode_CheckConsistency both because of performance considerations and because it may introduce subtle behavioral changes in code paths that did not lock before.

That rationale makes sense. The reason I suggested using a critical section is that `_PyUnicode_CheckConsistency` checks a number of different fields on the unicode object. I'm not very familiar with the internals of unicode objects, so I'm not sure which of those fields are mutable or if the logic in `_PyUnicode_CheckConsistency` requires an atomic view of all of the fields. For example, in some cases `_PyUnicode_CheckConsistency` will iterate over the data:

https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/8eebe4e6d02bb4ad3f1ca6c52624186903dce893/Objects/unicodeobject.c#L723-L724

I think we probably need an atomic view of data and length for that loop to be correct.

I don't think those need atomic operations. Those fields are generally initialized on creation and are immutable for the lifetime of the `str`. Operations like `PyUnicode_Resize()` may modify the string, but only if the object has one reference.

The "mutable" fields that may be modified while other threads are accessing the string object are:

* `hash` - lazily initialized
* `state.interned` - may be interned after creation
* `utf8` (in `PyCompactUnicodeObject`) - lazily initialized for non-ascii strings (requires memory order "acquire" to read)
* `utf8_length` - initialized together with `utf8` (and written *before* `utf8`)
